summary: A path tells a command where a file or folder is. An absolute path starts at / and always means the same place. A relative path starts from the folder you are in.
notes: /home/student/cs/project/src is absolute: it starts at / (the top of the file system) and works no matter where you are.
In ../cs/project, .. means the folder above music, which is /home/student.
~/music is short for /home/student/music, so it works from any folder.
pitfall: A relative path depends on where you are. ls src works inside cs/project but fails in music with ls: cannot access 'src': No such file or directory. Run pwd to check where you are.
